paragrafos: **Three measurements side by side, never added together.** Two prediction markets (Polymarket and Kalshi), voting-intention polls checked against the official notice filed with the Commission des sondages, and French press coverage. The first round is on April 18 and the runoff on May 2, 2027.

**On 11/10/2026, the two markets and the polls measure different things about Marine Le Pen.** In the win contract, Polymarket pays 45.25 and Kalshi 49.00. In polls with fieldwork up to 10/22, she is first in all 55 first-round lists of the last 45 days, from 8 pollsters, at 31% to 38%, and leads in the 26 runoff match-ups in which she was tested, at 52% to 70%. Her appeal to the Cour de cassation against her ineligibility is due to be ruled on by early April 2027.

**The market puts David Lisnard right behind Le Pen; the polls do not.** In the win contract, Lisnard is 2nd on Polymarket, at 13.95, and on Kalshi he is at 13.00, the same last price as Jean-Luc Mélenchon. In the polls, his average is 7.0 across 12 lists from 7 pollsters over the last 30 days, and he did not place in the top two in any of the 13 lists of the last 45 days in which he appears.

**Behind Le Pen, the order in the polls is not the order in the market.** Jean-Luc Mélenchon is 2nd in the poll average, at 16.5 across 38 lists from 7 pollsters, and places in the top two in 42 of the 55 lists of the last 45 days; in the 9 runoff match-ups in which he was tested, he trails in all of them, at 30% to 34%. In the win contract, he is 3rd on Polymarket, at 13.50, and at 13.00 on Kalshi. Raphaël Glucksmann and Édouard Philippe share the same 30-day average, 13.9, across 36 and 27 lists; in the lists of the last 45 days in which they appear, Philippe places in the top two in 10 of 39, and Glucksmann in 3 of 45. In the win contract, Philippe is at 9.50 on Polymarket and 7.30 on Kalshi, and Glucksmann at 2.35 and 4.00.

**In the French press on 11/09, six of the ten headlines collected are about Teddy Riner's candidacy.** Libération reports that the judoka announces his run for president; Les Echos, Le Figaro, BFMTV and Ouest-France, the latter in two headlines, cover the effect on the campaign, how the French are reacting and his platform. In the win contract, Riner is at 2.55 on Polymarket and 2.00 on Kalshi; in the Polymarket contract on whether he will be on the ballot, 25.00. No poll list in the structured database has tested him so far, and the most recent published fieldwork is from 10/22.

**What this screen does not do.** It does not add or average the two markets, it does not turn a price into a voting intention, and it does not show a poll number without its checked official notice. On the Saturday and Sunday of each round, polls and prices are frozen, as French law of 1977 requires.
